--- title: "Salary value: who is over- or underpaid?" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"} ## Takeaways - **The old ratio rule labeled most players.** The notebook's rule (predicted ÷ actual salary above 1.2 or below 0.8) called 38% of NBA veterans underpaid and 36% overpaid. With 90% intervals, only 5% and 5% are clearly over- or underpaid; for everyone else the difference is within the model's uncertainty. - **Max contracts can't be judged against the market.** The old rule called 69% of NBA max-contract players overpaid, but max pay is capped by the league's rules, so their market value is never observed. They're shown by value delivered instead. - **Minimum contracts are underpaid by design**, especially late-season prorated deals. - **Injuries:** each overpay is split into a part from games missed and a part from performance. ::: ## How it works - **Pay scale:** salary as a share of an average team payroll in that league-season. This puts the NBA, WNBA and every season on one scale without typing in salary-cap figures. - **Seasons:** NBA 2009-10 onward, WNBA 2021 onward (when salary data is complete). - **Fair pay:** a gradient-boosting model of pay, trained only on **veteran** contracts, because rookie-scale, minimum and max salaries are set by rules. Inputs: lineup-based offense and defense impact (this season and last), minutes (this season and last), availability, age, position and archetype. More impact, minutes or availability never lowers fair pay. Each player's own season is held out when predicting him. - **Surplus:** log(fair pay) − log(actual pay); above 0 = underpaid. Never a ratio. - **Interval:** a 90% band for fair pay, calibrated on held-out seasons (it covers 90% of NBA and WNBA veteran contracts). A player is labeled only when the whole band is on one side of zero. - **Low-salary shrinkage:** the surplus on cheap contracts was shrunk by a factor tuned with cross-validation (does the shrunk surplus predict the pay change at a player's next contract?). The tuning chose **no shrinkage**, so cheap contracts are instead kept in their own cohort. - **Contract cohorts:** rookie scale (draft history, plus inferred for 2024+ draftees), minimum scale (identical low amounts paid to many players, or prorated deals), max scale (identical top-tier amounts), veteran. ## Old rule vs new rule Share of player-seasons labeled over- or underpaid. ```{=html}
